title: Conformance matrix, Phase 6 (the five-function core as a system: scenarios, scale, failure injection, soak)
note: Same rules as the other matrices. 'verified' = tests pass and a real independent peer (UERANSIM, Open5GS's AUSF / NRF) confirms it. The system rows are run by deploy/run/g5c-cluster.sh (real processes) and nf/amf/tests/load_core.c; the gap rows are what the phase leaves out.

rows.procedure: S1: initial registration with 5G-AKA, security mode, GUTI allocation, then UE-initiated de-registration; every function a separate process (udr, UDM, AUSF-lite, PCF, UPF, SMF, AMF), a scripted gNB over real SCTP and a scripted UE that derives every key itself
rows.evidence: deploy/run/g5c-cluster.sh ns load: every UE completes and the UE-context, SMF-session and UPF-session counts read from /metrics return to their starting values. UERANSIM does the same against our AMF with Open5GS's AUSF / NRF (oracle S1-S3).

rows.procedure: S2: S1 plus UE-requested PDU session establishment, user plane through the UPF (N3 GTP-U to N6) and release at de-registration
rows.evidence: UERANSIM's UE pings through our UPF with our AMF, SMF, UDM and PCF (oracle S2, 0% loss); the scripted gNB and UE do the same with checked tunnel identifiers and addresses.

rows.procedure: S3: S2 plus UE-requested PDU session release and re-registration with the 5G-GUTI
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 with every function ours except the AUSF and NRF (Open5GS's).

rows.procedure: S4: policy change while the session is up: PCF update -> SMF -> N4 modification -> NAS modification command -> N2 modify request
rows.evidence: Oracle S4 against our AMF, SMF, UPF, UDM and PCF; UERANSIM's gNB does not answer a modify request, so the NGAP request in the capture is the evidence there and the scripted gNB completes the procedure.

rows.procedure: S5: connection release (inactivity), the UE returns with a service request, user plane resumes; network-triggered paging for downlink data
rows.evidence: Oracle S5 (nr-cli ue-release, then ping); paging, its repetition and its failure with the scripted gNB.

rows.procedure: 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 simulated UEs, each registering with 5G-AKA and establishing a PDU session, then de-registering; the functions in one process on real sockets (load_core)
rows.evidence: 10,000 UEs over 32 gNBs: all registered with a session in 71 s, de-registered in 17 s, latency p50 9 ms / 195 ms (registration / session), no descriptor leak, AMF, SMF and UPF empty at the end. Run with G5C_LOAD_UES=10000; ctest runs 150.

rows.procedure: the same load against the daemons as separate processes in a private network namespace (deploy/run/g5c-cluster.sh ns load)
rows.evidence: 10,000 UEs over 32 gNBs: registered with a session each in 20.7 s (484 UE/s), de-registered in 9.8 s; latency p50 38 ms / 25 ms / 29 ms (registration / session / de-registration), flat as the population grows. ctest runs 300 UEs x 2 waves.

rows.procedure: the unauthenticated-connection limit counts only connections that have not completed authentication
rows.evidence: Found by the first load run: the limit counted every connection, so an AMF refused new UEs with an overload Error Indication once 4,096 UEs were connected.

rows.procedure: network functions killed (SIGKILL) and restarted at random while the load runs; afterwards a clean wave of new UEs must pass in every detail
rows.evidence: 30 s of load with 16 kills (UPF, SMF, AMF, UDM, PCF, AUSF, UDR): 8,762 UE cycles completed, the rest counted as failures, no hang; the recovery wave of 100 UEs passes.

rows.procedure: SMF restart: sessions come back from the state file, the UPF association is re-established with the same Recovery Time Stamp
rows.evidence: In-process test with the real PFCP sockets; the chaos run restarts the SMF as a process.

rows.procedure: UPF restart detected through the Recovery Time Stamp: sessions released towards the AMF and the N4 association set up again
rows.evidence: Found by the chaos run: the association was not re-established, so the UPF refused new sessions (cause 72).

rows.procedure: AMF restart: registered UEs come back CM-IDLE with their security context and are served by a service request
rows.evidence: In-process test; the chaos run restarts the AMF as a process.

rows.procedure: loss of the N2 association: UE contexts of that gNB go CM-IDLE, sessions are kept
rows.evidence: Scripted gNB closes its SCTP association.

rows.procedure: UDR outage and restart under UDM / PCF load: a clean 503 while it is down, the first request after it is back succeeds, no leaked state
rows.evidence: soak_core stops and restarts the UDR repeatedly under a mixed workload (also under ASan and TSan).

rows.procedure: subscriber store persistence is a snapshot plus a journal of changed subscribers: a crash image recovers every flushed change, removals included, and a journal older than its snapshot is not replayed
rows.evidence: test_journal_recovery copies the files of a running store (what a crash leaves) and reopens them.

rows.procedure: waves of register / session / de-register for a fixed time against the daemons; RSS of every function must stay flat between the second and the last wave
rows.evidence: ns soak 500 UEs for 90 s (30 waves): no function grows beyond the tolerance; ctest runs 30 s. The strategy's 72 hour run uses the same command (`ns soak 500 259200`).

rows.procedure: memory and descriptor leaks: the load run under ASan/UBSan (leak check at exit) and the chaos run
rows.evidence: load_core under AddressSanitizer reports nothing at exit; descriptors return to their starting count (+ the bounded SBI connection pool).

rows.procedure: 72 hour soak
rows.evidence: The harness exists and ran for minutes in this environment; the 72 hour run needs a host that can be left alone for three days (`ns soak 500 259200`).

rows.procedure: S1-S8 on srsRAN (ZMQ gNB / UE) and an O-RAN emulator
rows.evidence: Deferred by the owner until all eleven functions exist; the interop pass with srsUE and the OCUDU gNB is planned for that point together with the demo environment.

rows.procedure: scripted UEs do not run user-plane traffic at scale (control plane and session setup only)
rows.evidence: UPF throughput is measured by its own benchmark (about 3.2 Gbit/s uplink, 1.8 Gbit/s downlink per core); a combined signalling + traffic run needs a traffic generator inside the namespace.

rows.procedure: an SMF killed within the write-behind window of its state file leaves PFCP sessions on the UPF that the restarted SMF does not know
rows.evidence: The window is 25 ms or ten times the cost of a write. A graceful stop flushes. Closing it needs an N4 session audit (a Recovery Time Stamp change is not usable because the SMF keeps the stamp to keep its sessions).
